subtopic: Tree and Graph Traversals (BFS, DFS, Dijkstra, A*)
question_text: Why does Dijkstra's shortest path algorithm fail or produce incorrect results on graphs containing negative edge weights?

options.text: It uses a FIFO queue instead of a priority queue
Its greedy choice assumes that visiting an unvisited node with minimal current distance permanently settles its optimal shortest path
It cannot handle directed cyclic graphs
It requires all vertices to have an even degree

answer_explanation: Dijkstra greedily marks nodes as permanently visited once dequeued from the min-heap, assuming any subsequent path extension will only increase the total cost. A negative edge later in the graph violates this monotonic distance growth assumption.
reference_solution: Correct Choice: B. Rationale: Dijkstra greedily marks nodes as permanently visited once dequeued from the min-heap, assuming any subsequent path extension will only increase the total cost. A negative edge later in the graph violates this monotonic distance growth assumption.
